quote_item10: Всего в исследовании приняли участие 1 000 респондентов из 22 муниципальных районов и г.о. Саранск, в общей сложности охвачено более 80 населённых пунктов. Выборка квотная, репрезентует структуру жителей субъекта по полу, возрасту и типу расселения [EN: In total 1,000 respondents from 22 municipal districts and the Saransk urban district took part in the study, covering more than 80 settlements. notes: Item 6 HIGH: an author-stated conceptual definition with no external ground truth — respondents self-report encountering whatever they personally judge to be 'fake news', so the case definition is the respondent's, not an external standard. Item 10 LOW: denominator is the full 1,000-respondent quota sample of a defined regional population, which is the quantity a self-reported recall-prevalence claim implies. quote_item6: Coders rated each video on a 5-point Likert scale adapted from Tam et. al for misinformation, i.e., 1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = neutral, 4 = agree, 5 = strongly agree that the video contained misinformation8. A score > 3 indicated the TikTok video contained misinformation.
quote_item10: The videos were ranked by engagement, defined as the summed number of likes, comments, and shares. The top twenty videos were selected for further review as shown in Figure 1.
notes: Item 6 HIGH: misinformation is a subjective 5-point agreement rating by two specialists with no external ground truth — exactly the author-devised, internal-and-ad-hoc case definition the ruling still fails; the study's other instrument (DISCERN) is a quality scale and cannot stand in for falsity. Item 10 HIGH: denominator is 74 top-engagement videos across four hashtags — a doubly curated (topical + top-N-by-engagement) content corpus. Item 3 HIGH: top-twenty-by-engagement selection. Item 7 HIGH: no reliability statistic for the misinformation rating (DISCERN's validation does not transfer). Item 9 HIGH: a single-timepoint hashtag scrape generalised to 'prevalence of misinformation'. Items 4-5 NA (content analysis).

quote_item6: Three authors, LAS, AM, EA, group coded five articles to create the codebook. Using the final codebook, we coded an initial subset of 20 articles for interrater reliability (Krippendorf's alpha = 0.811).

notes: Item 6 HIGH: the misinformation categories are an author-built codebook developed by the three coders themselves, including an "otherwise obviously false statement" catch-all — internal and ad hoc, with no external claim list or fact-check verdicts as anchor. Reliability being good (alpha = 0.811) makes item 7 LOW but does not supply an external case definition. Items 1-3 HIGH (topic-curated, top-N-by-engagement frame). Items 4-5 NA (content analysis). Item 9 LOW (2019-2021 stated).

quote_item6: Misinformation was defined as posts stating factually incorrect information. Screeners evaluated the content of the posts for validity, opened all embedded links, and assessed the post's tone.
quote_item10: From the pertinent posts of timeframe 1, 8014 (70.1%) were deemed factual and 3422 (29.9%) were deemed misinformation.
notes: Item 6 HIGH: falsity is decided by trained study-team screeners against no external standard — no fact-check verdicts, no credibility list, and the authors add that "The intent of the poster was a key consideration", which imports motive into a falsity judgement. Item 10 HIGH: denominators are the keyword-screened, topic-relevant post sets (11,436 and 5,982) for a single COVID-vaccine-and-fertility niche; the 29.9% -> 45.1% rise is a share of that curated topical corpus and cannot speak to audience exposure. Items 1-2 HIGH (keyword-seeded topical universe). Item 3 LOW: a full census of the keyword-matching posts in the COVID-19-TweetIDs corpus, not top-N selection. Item 7 HIGH: no kappa or alpha reported, only group consensus on ambiguous posts. Items 4-5 NA (content analysis).
